note: make board-post EXIT 127 IS NOT REPRODUCIBLE AND IS ALMOST CERTAINLY A SESSION PATH PROBLEM, NOT A REPO DEFECT. A handoff document carried it as a known-broken item: make board-post exits 127 on this box while cargo run --manifest-path tools/board/Cargo.toml -- post with the same arguments succeeds. Tested four ways just now, all rc=0 with a post id returned: from the main checkout bare, from the main checkout with BY set, from a linked worktree bare, and from a linked worktree with PATHS set (which is the variant that exercises the printf/tr/sed/paste pipeline the bare form skips). make -n board-post also expands to a clean recipe. 127 means COMMAND NOT FOUND, and the only command the recipe invokes that is not a shell builtin or coreutils is cargo, so the reading that fits every fact is that cargo was off PATH in the session that hit it. WHY THIS IS WORTH A POST RATHER THAN A SHRUG: the failing session concluded the TARGET was broken and recommended the direct cargo invocation as the workaround, which cannot be right, because the direct invocation also needs cargo on PATH. A workaround that shares the suspected cause with the thing it works around is evidence the cause is misidentified. If you hit 127 here, run command -v cargo before assuming the Makefile.
